subject: Re: Dedicated capacity GPU alignment — memory vs perf anchors for DS-4721
message_1_subject: Dedicated capacity planning: our workload memory profile + ask
message_1_body:
Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We ran a quick export of representative inference traces and attached a small sample (datasurge-workload-sample.csv). High level: most requests are short chat-style prompts (~30–80 tokens) but we have a 7% tail of long retrieval-heavy prompts that open large contexts (70k tokens when fully expanded). Latency SLO is 200ms p95 for short chats; for long context it can be higher but we need completion correctness.

Primary asks:
- Guidance on whether we should anchor Dedicated on H100 for large-context headroom vs A100 to save cost.
- If a hybrid approach (L4 for short chat, H100 for long) is viable operationally and how switchover/fallthrough would look.
- Any quick back-of-envelope on expected token cost delta (H100 vs A100 vs L4) given our mix.

I can join a technical sync if helpful.

Best,
Amalie
VP Infrastructure, DataSurge
message_2_subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning: our workload memory profile + ask
message_2_body:
Amalie — thanks for the data and clear asks. Quick take before we schedule a deep dive: 

- Anchoring on H100: Recommended if you want a single dedicated pool that handles the 7% heavy-context tail without complex routing. H100 provides large HBM and faster FP16 throughput which helps KV cache for long-context models (e.g., 70k token effective contexts). The tradeoff: roughly 2–2.5x higher per-GPU cost vs A100 for reserved capacity.

- Anchoring on A100: Good middle ground if you can live with a small degradation on the heaviest contexts and prefer lower committed spend. A100 still supports high batch throughput and larger mixed-precision memory footprints but may need more aggressive KV eviction or model sharding for the 70k cases.

- L4 as primary + fallthrough: Very cost-effective for the short-chat 93% of traffic. L4 is much cheaper and excels on small-context, low-latency generation. Operationally we'd route by request classifier (prompt length + retrieval size). Critical caveat: L4 memory limits mean you must redirect long-context requests to an H100/A100 pool — that introduces cross-pool routing and slightly higher end-to-end latency for those requests.

Next step proposal: Jordan and I will run the sample through our internal profiling to produce a 3-sku cost/latency matrix (H100 / A100 / L4) and a recommended fleet mix with fallthrough ratios. Expect that by EOD tomorrow. Attaching a short template of what we will produce.

- Sofia
Director, Strategic Deals, Redwood Inference
message_3_subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning: our workload memory profile + ask
message_3_body:
Amalie — added a couple of practical points from ops/serving side: 

1) KV cache hit patterns: if your retrieval pipeline sends dense context segments frequently re-used across users, H100's larger HBM reduces remote KV fetches (less CPU/GPU cross-talk). For 70k expanded contexts with overlapping vectors, H100 can cut token compute by ~10–20% vs A100 because you can keep more layers of cached state locally.

2) Autoscaling and burst: if you anchor on A100 or H100, we recommend keeping a small L4 reserved pool for day-to-day peaks and warm L4 instances for sub-50-token requests to reduce p95 latency. This hybrid reserved+burst model often lowers overall committed spend.

3) Quantization: if the long-context model tolerates INT8-like quant, A100 and some H100 builds can use q8* kernels to reduce memory pressure. That can tilt the choice toward A100 in cost-sensitive deals but requires evaluation.

I'll run the sample through our latency/cost profiler and include per-token cost estimates in the matrix Sofia mentioned.

—Jordan
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
message_4_subject: DataSurge proposal: SKU mix scenario + numbers (DS-4721)
message_4_body:
Amalie — attached is the short proposal (proposal-DS-4721.pdf) plus our model workbook (redwood-sku-cost-model.xlsx) with three scenarios: H100-anchor, A100-anchor, and L4-primary with H100 fallthrough. Summaries below: 

Scenario A — H100-anchor (single pool)
- Rationale: simplest ops surface, handles 100% of requests including the 7% long-context without cross-pool routing.
- Fleet: 12 H100s reserved (baseline), 3 H100 burst
- Estimated committed monthly cost (reserved): $112k
- Expected p95 short-chat latency: ~120–160ms; long-context completion latency improves due to HBM headroom
- Risk: higher committed spend; potential underutilization if long-context growth doesn't materialize

Scenario B — A100-anchor (single pool)
- Rationale: lowers committed spend while giving decent long-context support with modest KV tuning.
- Fleet: 18 A100s reserved, 6 A100 burst
- Estimated committed monthly cost (reserved): $62k
- Expected p95 short-chat latency: ~140–200ms; long-context may need sharding/eviction strategies
- Risk: may need operational work to preserve quality on 70k cases

Scenario C — L4-primary + H100 fallthrough (hybrid)
- Rationale: minimizes committed spend while preserving quality for large contexts through targeted routing.
- Fleet: 10 L4 reserved, 4 H100 reserved for fallthrough, 2 H100 burst
- Estimated committed monthly cost (reserved): $29k (L4) + $38k (H100) = ~$67k
- Expected p95 short-chat latency: ~50–90ms on L4; long-context routed to H100 with 1–2x higher end-to-end latency due to routing but better cost efficiency overall
- Risk: added routing complexity, cross-pool tracing and SLO reasoning; needs request classifier and staged rollouts

Recommendation: For DataSurge's mix, Scenario C gives the best cost/perf balance if you're willing to accept an ops split and implement classifier-based routing. Scenario B is an acceptable compromise if you prefer single-pool simplicity and lower ops overhead. Scenario A is recommended only if you prioritize single-pool simplicity and expect long-context growth >10% soon.

Next steps: if you want, we can (1) run 48-hour pilot with Scenario C traffic split of 90/10 (L4/H100) using your sample traces, (2) instrument SLO dashboards and KV cache metrics, and (3) produce a final commercial commitment worksheet to fold into DS-4721.

Would you like us to schedule the pilot starting next Monday?

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
